summary: Embedding orientation mismatch combined with router-hash change causing degraded rerank quality and tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer QueryFlow reports sudden degradation in rerank relevance plus elevated p95 token latency from the reranking endpoint after an internal rolling change. Symptoms include: unexpected ordering changes in top-k results, higher tail latency for rerank requests, and intermittent 503s from the embed->rerank handoff. Impact: production traffic from QueryFlow (enterprise) sees 6-12% drop in expected top-5 recall for critical search flows and p95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~670ms.

Impact:
- Business-critical search feature experiencing visible quality regressions for end users (query samples attached).
- Elevated tail latency causing timeouts in QueryFlow application (some automated retries observed).

Environment:
- prod-us-east, customer tenant: queryflow-prod, routed via proxy-router cluster pr-us1.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/embeddings (text-embed-xl-v2), /v1/rerank (rerank-lite-v1).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send sample query set (provided in attachment) to embeddings endpoint pinned to text-embed-xl-v2 with tenant header X-Tenant: queryflow-prod.
2) Call rerank endpoint using returned embeddings without additional normalization.
3) Observe top-5 ordering vs baseline stored in QueryFlow eval set and check p95 latency on reranker traces.

Observed behavior:
- Non-deterministic top-k reordering compared to baseline; several queries show inversion of relevant candidates.
- Reranker logs show occasional fallback to CPU path due to upstream embed shape/metadata mismatch and router re-sharding events.
- Proxy-router logs show frequent 502/503s for the embed->rerank internal RPC during a 30m window.

Expected behavior:
- Stable top-k ordering for the same input and consistent p95 latency within SLOs (<=300ms).

Relevant logs/metrics (high level):
- spike in embed-service 500s at 2026-03-10T03:40Z correlating with router rolling update.
- reranker p95 increased to 670ms between 03:40Z-04:10Z.
- embed payload inspection shows alternating orientation flag values (row-major vs column-major) in metadata header on some requests.
comments: 2026-03-10 14:05 - Support (Asha Patel): Initial triage: asked customer for example queries, tenant headers, and whether they are pinning versions. Customer replied with sample bundle (attached) and noted they observed behavior starting approx 03:40 UTC.

2026-03-10 15:10 - Eng (Marcus Chen): Noted a router config rollout was executed in us-east around 03:35Z (PR referenced). Requested router and embed-service logs for 03:30Z-04:30Z. Assigned to serving-runtime and proxy-router oncall.

2026-03-11 09:22 - SRE (Leila Moreno): Found router hash ring change at 03:37Z that coincided with re-sharding events. Some embed requests had missing 'embed-orientation' header after proxy sidecar upgrade; these defaulted to legacy orientation interpretation and triggered downstream shape conversion and CPU fallback.

2026-03-12 11:41 - Customer (QueryFlow - James Lin): Confirmed that their client SDK did not include explicit normalization header; they rely on platform defaults. Asked for mitigation steps and whether hotfix can be provided.

2026-03-13 08:03 - Eng (Marcus Chen): Implemented a quick mitigation in staging to coerce missing orientation headers to the expected default and added a compatibility shim in proxy-router. Preparing canary in prod-us-east.

2026-03-13 12:50 - Support (Asha Patel): Communicated mitigation plan to customer and schedule for canary rollout at 2026-03-13T16:00Z. Requested that customer hold off config changes during canary window.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Router hash ring change produced transient re-routing to replicas with older embed-service build that emits different orientation header formatting; this caused selective downstream CPU fallback and slight numerical drift in embeddings.

Hypothesis 2: Proxy sidecar upgrade inadvertently strips or renames 'embed-orientation' metadata header (observed in logs) for ~8% of requests, triggering a fallback normalization path in reranker that is slow and nondeterministic.

Evidence: Correlation between router rolling update time and spike in embed-service 500s and reranker p95. Packet capture and header dump show alternating presence/absence of 'x-embed-orientation' on affected requests.

Partial reproduction: Replayed affected customer bundle against staging proxy-router with the sidecar image from the rollout and reproduced top-k inversion on 3/25 test queries; enabling shim to add default header resolved ordering and reduced p95 back to ~240ms.
Next steps: schedule controlled canary in prod-us-east, roll forward proxy-router compatibility shim, and backfill integration tests for header preservation across router + sidecar.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-13): Canary deployment of proxy-router compatibility shim that injects missing 'x-embed-orientation: row-major' for unannotated requests. Canary metric snapshot shows reranker p95 returned to baseline (~230ms) for QueryFlow traffic and top-k recall recovered in sampled queries.

Planned permanent fix: Merge PR to router and sidecar to preserve embed metadata headers across re-shards and add explicit header requirement to embedding API; scheduled release 2026-03-18 after QA.
- Add non-regression test in CI to verify embed header propagation across proxy-router rolling updates.
- Notify customer of the permanent fix schedule and offer post-deployment validation run.

Follow-up: Create an internal post-incident note linking this ticket, the router PR, and the embed-service test failures. Recommend updating runbook to include header-preservation checks during rolling updates.
